title: Active host grid has two persisted sources of truth, with a synthetic 'Default' environment papering over the seam
existing_state: Every SaveConfiguration writes the live grid to two places in the same config.json: the active EnvironmentConfig.Hosts (Form1.cs:14630-14633 → EnvironmentService.SaveCurrentGridToEnvironment) and SavedState.Hosts via BuildApplicationState (Form1.cs:14679-14686). Nothing in the model layer ties them together — reconciliation is Form1 convention. The seam is bridged by a synthetic environment: 'Default' is not stored in the Environments map at all until a 'first adoption' event; until then BuildLegacyDefaultEnvironment regenerates it on demand from SavedState (ConfigurationService.cs:202-206, EnvironmentConfig.FromApplicationState:26-46). Because FromApplicationState carries no Variables, GetEnvironment("Default") before adoption always returns an environment with empty Variables — Default-environment variables conceptually cannot exist until some unrelated action (creating an env, EnvironmentService.cs:162-165; saving a non-Default env, :126-129; importing, :338-341; or a variable write while Default is active, :282-285) materializes it. Beyond the behavioral trap, the duplication roughly doubles the persisted grid payload and any future feature that reads hosts must know which copy wins when.
recommendation: Make the Environments map the single source of truth for host-grid data: materialize 'Default' into the map once at load time (one-shot migration from SavedState, mirroring the existing legacy-preset migration pattern), drop Hosts/HostColumns/SelectedHostIndices from ApplicationState, and have SaveConfiguration write the grid only through EnvironmentService. SavedState then shrinks to genuine UI state (selection, last CSV path, preset choice).
user_benefit: Removes a whole category of 'which copy is real' bugs (empty Default variables, grid/environment drift after partial saves), shrinks config.json, and halves the grid data serialized on every save.
